name: Generate SEO blog posts with Claude and publish drafts to WordPress

parameters.content:
## Generate SEO blog posts with Claude and publish drafts to WordPress

### How it works

This workflow collects a blog post request, fetches a reference article, and uses Claude to generate a structured SEO-focused outline. It then expands the outline into section copy, adds a summary, SEO metadata, and FAQs, combines everything into final HTML, and creates a draft post in WordPress. If the outline cannot be normalized or validated, it returns an error message instead of publishing.

### Setup steps

- Open **Set Article Parameters** and enter your reference article URL, target audience, and tone of voice. The form already collects keywords, section count, and target word count.
- Add Anthropic credentials for the Claude outline, section-writing, and SEO/FAQ generation nodes.
- Add WordPress credentials and confirm the target site, post type, draft status, title field, and content field mappings are correct.
- Ensure the reference article URL is publicly accessible or reachable by the n8n instance.
- Activate the workflow and open the form URL to submit your first request.

### Customization

Adjust the configured section_count, max_words, keywords, Claude prompts, SEO/FAQ format, and WordPress publishing options such as categories, tags, author, or whether posts remain drafts.

## Collect blog request

Starts the workflow from a form submission and prepares the core article settings used throughout the generation process.

## Analyze reference article

Fetches the provided reference article and extracts a lightweight structure, including headings, sample paragraphs, and counts, to guide the new post.

## Generate article outline

Uses an AI agent backed by the Anthropic chat model to create an article outline from the request settings and parsed reference structure.

## Validate outline data

Normalizes the AI outline into clean JSON fields and checks whether the output is valid before the workflow continues.

## Create article sections

Branches into title and introduction preparation while also splitting the outline into individual sections, generating copy for each one, parsing the results, and merging the intro with section content.

## Build article body

Converts the merged introduction and generated sections into the main article HTML, with an intro paragraph followed by H2 section blocks.

## Generate SEO extras

Creates the quick summary, SEO fields, and FAQs with Claude, then parses them into HTML blocks for inclusion in the final post.

## Combine final HTML

Merges the main article body with the generated summary and FAQ content, then assembles the final HTML in reading order.

## Publish draft post

Creates the generated article as a WordPress draft and displays a success response to the requester.

## Show outline error

Displays an error message when the outline validation branch fails, preventing draft creation with incomplete or malformed content.

parameters.formTitle: Create a WordPress blog post with AI
parameters.formDescription: Enter your keywords and choose the article length. A draft post will be created in WordPress.

assignments.name: target_audience
assignments.value: General readers who are new to the topic (awareness stage)

options.systemMessage:
=You are an expert content strategist and SEO blog planner.

Create a plan for one new blog article based on the target keywords in the user message.

AUDIENCE AND TONE
- Target audience: {{ $('Set Article Parameters').first().json.target_audience }}
- Tone of voice: {{ $('Set Article Parameters').first().json.tone_of_voice }}

REFERENCE ARTICLE STRUCTURE
The JSON below describes the structure of an article already published on the same site (title, headings, sample paragraphs and counts). It may be empty.
- Use it only as guidance for flow, pacing, depth and readability.
- Do not copy its wording, headings, examples or narrative.

{{ JSON.stringify($json.reference_structure || 'none') }}

RULES
1. Write one keyword-focused, curiosity-driven title of 65 characters or fewer.
2. Write an introduction of 2 to 3 sentences that opens with a broad trend, curiosity or question. It is published as the opening paragraph, so write it for the reader.
3. Create exactly {{ $('Set Article Parameters').first().json.section_count }} sections.
   - Each heading is a natural question people are likely to ask about the keywords.
   - Each section covers one clear benefit, concern, question or use case.
   - Sections must not overlap.
4. For each section, write a chapter_prompt of 1 to 2 sentences that tells the writer what to cover.
5. Do not write the full article.
6. Do not sound robotic, corporate or overly academic.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Return only one valid JSON object. No markdown, no code fences, no text before or after it.
Use exactly these keys:
{
  "title": "string",
  "introduction": "string",
  "sections": [
    { "heading": "string", "chapter_prompt": "string" }
  ]
}

parameters.responseText: There was a problem creating the article outline. Please refresh the form and try again.

values.content:
=You are an SEO editor. Read the article below and write supporting content for it.

Target keywords: {{ $('Set Article Parameters').first().json.keywords }}

ARTICLE HTML
{{ $json.article_html }}

Write the following:
1. quick_summary: a plain-text summary of the whole article in about 50 words. No heading, label, markdown or HTML.
2. seo_title: a clear, compelling title of 60 characters or fewer that includes the main keyword.
3. seo_description: a natural meta description of 140 to 155 characters. Compelling, not clickbait.
4. faqs: exactly 5 questions and answers.
   - Base the questions on the target keywords and on what a searcher would ask.
   - Every answer must be supported by the article. Do not invent facts.
   - Each answer is 1 to 3 sentences, in plain text.
   - Do not repeat the same idea across FAQs.

Output rules:
- Return only one valid JSON object. No markdown, no code fences, no text before or after it.
- Use exactly these keys:
{
  "quick_summary": "string",
  "seo_title": "string",
  "seo_description": "string",
  "faqs": [
    { "question": "string", "answer": "string" }
  ]
}
